The Hubble Space Telescope being deployed by the space shuttle Discovery. April 25, 1990.

The Hubble Space Telescope is a space telescope that was launched into low Earth orbit in 1990, and remains in operation. Although not the first space telescope, Hubble is one of the largest and most versatile, and is well known as both a vital research tool and a public relations boon for astronomy.

The HST is named after the astronomer Edwin Hubble who was an American astronomer who played a crucial role in establishing the field of extragalactic astronomy and is generally regarded as one of the most important observational cosmologists of the 20th century.

Hubble is the only telescope designed to be serviced in space by astronauts. Four Space Shuttle missions have repaired, upgraded, and replaced systems on the telescope and the final servicing mission was completed in 2009. The telescope could last until 2030–2040. Its successor, the James Webb Space Telescope is scheduled for launch in 2018.
